author: Mathew Richards
title: Bonita business owner pleads guilty to Medicare fraud scheme - NewsBreak
text: SAN DIEGO, California — Jacobo Melcer, an 85-year-old resident of Bonita, California, pleaded guilty in federal court to conspiring to defraud Medicare of millions and paying unlawful kickbacks for patient referrals. Melcer admitted to submitting over $5.88 million in false claims through his durable medical equipment companies. Melcer's plea agreement revealed that he paid more than $227,000 in kickbacks for Medicare beneficiary referrals and prescriptions, knowing the prescriptions were signed by physicians without legitimate doctor-patient relationships. He fraudulently billed Medicare $5,885,382 and received $3,479,303 in payments, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of California. As part of his guilty plea, Melcer agreed to forfeit and pay restitution of $3,479,303. Additionally, Melcer admitted to creating and selling two DME companies to a co-conspirator to conceal true ownership from Medicare, as the co-conspirator was suspended as a Medicare provider. Melcer's sentencing is set for October 10, 2025. The case is prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Blanca Quintero and investigated by the FBI and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General.
